subject: QA walkthrough - levels 2-4 and ground floor lobby

body.text: A pre-handover QA walkthrough of Harbourview Apartments was carried out on 5 June 2025 with the Karaka Construction site manager and the Apex Interiors foreman. Levels 2 to 4 and the ground floor lobby were reviewed. These notes record the architect's observations only and do not constitute a producer statement; a further walkthrough will be required prior to practical completion.

The general standard of interior finish is good and the apartments on level 4 present well, with paint, flooring and joinery largely complete. That said, the scribers to the aluminium joinery in units 4/1 and 4/2 show gaps of up to 4mm at head junctions where they have shrunk back or been cut short, and these are to be refitted or filled and repainted before the units are offered for reinspection. Apex Interiors advised the same scriber stock was used on level 3, so the contractor should check all level 3 units for the same issue.

On level 3 the corridoor walls have been repainted since our last visit but under the new LED lighting they still show sanding marks and patchy sheen along the southern run, and a further full finish coat is required rather than spot touch ups. Ceiling access panels sit flush and are acceptable.

In the level 2 lobby the door hardwear to the entry doors has been supplied in satin chrome where the finishes schedule calls for matt black, an unapproved subsitution that is to be reversed - correct levers and pull handles to be procured and fitted, and the schedule reissued to the hardware supplier for the remaining levels. Signage and letterboxes were not yet installed and were not reviewed.

In unit 3/6 the skirting mitres to the living room are open at several corners where they meet the accoustic sealant bead at the base of the IT wall, and require refitting and touch up paint. In the ground floor lobby the entry matwell frame sits proud of the tile finish by 3-4mm and presents a trip edge at the main entrance; this is to be re-set flush before handover. Bathrooms to levels 2 and 3 presented well with no items recorded.
QA documentation to come from Apex Interiors for the level 4 units prior to CCC. The final walkthrough is to be booked with this office once the above are closed out.

subject: Cladding junction review - blocks A, B and C

body.text: The following observations were made during a site visit to Rimu Terraces, 8 Rimu Lane, Papamoa on 24 June 2025 and do not constitute a producer statement. The purpose of the visit was a review of cladding junctions across blocks A, B and C with the Mako Builders site manager and the Duraclad Facades foreman. Weather overcast, no rain during the visit.
Block A

Cladding to block A is complete and the installation is generally of a good standard; the inter-storey flashings are correctly lapped and the horizontal joints read consistently across the elevation. The sealant used to the inter-storey joint is however a mid grey against the dark cladding, a colour mismatch that reads clearly from the street. While this is an aesthetic matter rather than a weathertightness one it remains an open action - Duraclad Facades are to price removal and replacement with a colour matched sealant and advise this office.
Block B

On the north elevation the vertical cladding joints do not align between ground and first floor, out by up to 15mm at unit B3 and lessening towards B1. The misalignment is visible from the shared driveway and the panels at B3 are to be re-set where fixings and framing allow; where they cannot be corrected the joint treatment is to be agreed with this office before closing in. Separately, at unit B4 the soffit to cladding junction carries a gap of approx 8mm with no closure strip or sealant, which will admit birds and moisture - to be closed off as per the standard soffit detail.
Block C

The head junction as built at the block C stair window differs from detail 7 on A5-301, with the building wrap dressed over rather than under the head flashing upstand. It is not clear on site whether this will drain as intended; the architect is to confirm acceptability of the as-built arrangement, and no further cladding is to proceed past this junction until confirmed. All other block C junctions opened for review matched the details.
A further review will be undertaken once the above are addressed. Duraclad are to provide their QA records for the completed elevations with the next progress claim. Photos held on file.
